candidates.label: A026-Z1 (B only: captured zombies plant FF1FCCCC decoy blocks with their own INT 86h)
candidates.change: B only (A = rev0). zom20a path (CX!=0): after its b/d INT87, mov ax,1FFFh; int 86h with DI=0, DF=1, DX=CCCCh -> 64 dwords FF 1F CC CC at 0FF04h..0003h (no code is ever loaded below 400h or above FC00h, and these pages hold no anchor of our 52h/400h lattice). b/d path (CX=0): the 0E070E17 CC counter-bomb INT87 (worth nothing, B052) is replaced by mov di,bx; and di,0FC00h; add di,0164h; mov ax,1FFFh; mov dx,0CCCCh; int 86h -> block [X+68h,X+168h), X=(own load+3) and FC00h: inside the zombie's own MIN_GAP zone, on pages 4k/4k+1 outside in-page 52h-67h of pages 4k, so it cannot hit loaded code or our anchors/workers. Zombie band math switched to 16-bit DIV (mov ax,si; xor dx,dx; mov cx,3C00h; div cx; mul cx; add ax,bp; mov al,0A2h; same AX), so both zombie paths reach phoenix_init on the same turn as rev0. B's own startup unchanged; B's FF 1F CC CC tail decoy kept. Second INT86 charge of each zombie still unused.

threatFindings.threat: Captured zombies arrive with 2 unused INT 86h charges each; rev0 never spends them
threatFindings.evidence: Static: zom20a-d binaries contain no INT 86h; Cpu.java int86 uses per-process bomb1 count. Z1 spends one per zombie and changes only searcher cohorts measurably (15xh2, ustgi).
threatFindings.impact: A free resource that costs no A/B turns; zombie timing can be kept identical by trimming the zombie band math.

threatFindings.threat: A captured zom20b/d knows its own load address (BX = load+3 from its 'mov bx,ax; add bx,3' prologue); zom20a does not (BX is churned by mul)
threatFindings.evidence: dis86 of zom20b/zom20d at 0139h and zom20a; Warrior.java sets AX = load offset. Used by Z1's b/d block.
threatFindings.impact: Gives a placement that is always clear of loaded code (MIN_GAP 1024). The own-location block's separate value was not ablated (hypothesis that it adds anything beyond the FF04-0003 block).

threatFindings.threat: Zombie INT86 can wipe other zombies or finish the b/d chain (capture the lower b/d zombie)
threatFindings.evidence: Static only: zombies load at least 1024 bytes from other code (War.java MIN_GAP), so a 256-byte block placed relative to the zombie's own location cannot reach another zombie. Each b/d has 4 identical EB F9 CC CC tails (live 3rd from top); capturing both from the top needs 2+2 INT87s plus 1 for zom20a = 5 charges, the team has 4 (A, B, zom20a, first b/d). A scanning loop could find the lower zombie but costs thousands of turns; not built.
threatFindings.impact: No cheap capture extension; card's INT86 value is decoy planting.

threatFindings.threat: 2B2Team1 starts its INT87 at A600h (after its own INT86 at A500h), so a block exactly at A600h would always absorb it
threatFindings.evidence: Static dis86 of TOM_2B2Team1 (A024 also). Not built: a fixed A600h block can land on A's or B's body while they are still in startup (~1.4% of battles), likely costing more than the ~+0.002 field gain.

recommendation: promote-candidate (low-medium confidence): Z1 (B only, 214 B, sha 16be94ae) passes the screen bar (ALL +0.0100, no clearly negative group, the screen-negative cohorts did not replicate in ustgi) and its mechanism replicates in two paired threat jobs (+0.061 on 2025 searchers, +0.042 on 2024-live searchers). Its gain overlaps dec0A/C2 for forward-from-0 searchers; the new part is the top-of-arena half that also catches backward searchers (segment_fault). Best use: add Z1's zombie-path edits to the planned C2-A + SD combination (Z1 touches only zombie_entry/zombie paths; SD's B edits are in phoenix_init and are compatible). Remaining free resource: each zombie's second INT86 charge.
